title: Brazen Daytime Shooting at Chicago Police Station
description:
Thankfully, no one was injured in the incident. 

The video is presented to provide genuine footage of police incidents to promote transparency in government while providing educational, informative and newsworthy content allowing viewers to examine and assess public safety material. 

Please click JOIN to help support our efforts to promote transparency in government and the actions of law enforcement.

As a reminder, all individuals are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law. 

The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. If you know someone in one of these videos, please treat them with respect and courtesy.

The world is full of misleading content related to law enforcement; accordingly, it's incredibly important to provide transparency, insight and context to educate and inform the public.

transcript.text: A black SUV comes to a stop in the middle of the street. What happened next would be a brazen daytime shooting directly across from where police officers were stationed. Multiple 911 callers reported the shooting. There was a shooting at Monticello and the 606 at Bloomingdale. There was just a black SUV that just fired a couple of shots out of their car. It looks like there's a guy down. On the morning of November 1st, a group of police officers were meeting with community leaders, at a police substation near Monticello Avenue. At the same time, a man sat in his parked car waiting to pick up a family member. Minutes later, a black SUV drove down the avenue, then stopped in the street next to the parked car. Suddenly, three armed suspects exited the SUV and opened the victim's car door. One suspect walked back to the SUV and checked the surrounding area, possibly unaware a group of officers were in a building directly across the street. a suspect forcibly removed the driver from the vehicle and began rummaging through the victim's pockets. Officers in the police substation across the street heard an individual yelling for help outside. When officers responded to the commotion, they observed the three subjects engaged in the robbery. The victim fell to the ground as the suspects ran back to the SUV. One of the suspects fired a weapon in the direction of the officers, who then returned fire, shattering the passenger side window. As the SUV sped away, another shot was fired in the direction of the officers who dove for cover. After the incident, the police officers went to check on the victim, who incredibly avoided being shot and was uninjured. Thankfully, no one was injured in the shootout. As of the time of publication, the suspects in the incident are still outstanding. If anyone has information related to this incident, which occurred near 1800s, North Monticello Avenue. Please contact the Chicago Civilian Office of Police Accountability at 312-746-3609. By law, all police-involved shootings in Chicago are independently investigated by the Chicago Civilian Office of Police Accountability.
